faq.q: How long does a move to S/4HANA actually take?
faq.a: It depends on the number of entities, how much custom code you carry, and whether the work is regulated. A single-entity Grow implementation is measured in weeks. A multi-country programme with validation runs in waves across quarters. The assessment gives you a sequence and an effort range for your specific landscape rather than an industry average.

faq.q: Do we have to replace everything at once?
faq.a: No. Most programmes run in waves: a template first, then a pilot site, then rollout. Coexistence between ECC and S/4HANA during the transition is a normal pattern, and part of the plan is deciding which entities move first and why.

faq.q: What happens to the e-invoice requirement?
faq.a: It is handled inside the ERP as configuration. Government e-invoice work for Malaysia is a named service line in our portfolio, so it is scoped as part of the finance core rather than bolted on afterwards.

faq.q: We already have an SAP partner. Is this a replacement conversation?
faq.a: Not necessarily. We are independent and unbiased, and a common starting point is a second read on a plan you already have. If your current partner is doing well, the assessment will say so.

faq.q: Who actually does the work, and where do they sit?
faq.a: Delivery leads based in Kuala Lumpur and Singapore, backed by more than 400 consultants across Asia and 1,500 worldwide. The people in the assessment are the people in the workshops.

Hypercare first, then AMS and run support, including local issues at overseas sites. More than 95% of our client relationships are long term, which only happens if the run phase is taken as seriously as the build.
